bundle.note: FL-9's GUARD (BOB, 2026-09-10, answering DIST's DELEGATION). This member deliberately had NO build step: wrangler.jsonc recorded that the SOURCE deploys, because a committed bundle is a second place its version lives and an artifact that can drift from its source. That objection is ANSWERED rather than overruled — the recipe lives in bio-plane/scripts/fleet-bundle.mjs, the committed manifest beside the artifact states its sha256 and the sha256 of every input, and bio-plane/test/system/fleetbundles.test.mjs FAILS on a stale artifact rather than letting it ship. The forcing fact is DIST's: `newgroup` is a Worker, it cannot run wrangler or bundle, and this member is THREE modules, so a one-part upload cannot resolve them. This member still depends on NOTHING from npm; the build resolves esbuild from the plane's install.

note: The fleet-member marker. bio-plane/scripts/fleet-bundle.mjs discovers a fleet member by this file and builds and verifies its `bundle`; the member's suites in `testDir` are run by the package's own `npm test` (every `test/*.test.mjs`, the regression workflow's step for this package), because a member whose suite nothing executes is a component going dark. `surface` names the member's declared surface table in `entry` (fleet rule 2: no surface op may declare `mutating: true` — a member ASSERTS nothing); the fleet-coverage instrument that read it (scripts/coverage.mjs, D-117) is retired (K739), and the member's own suites now hold the surface (R34): both routes, and every other refused.
